nfc: nxp-nci: unregister without holding the mode mutex

NCI unregister can call the close operation and flush work that takes info_lock. Holding that same mutex across unregister deadlocks an open device.

Unregister first without info_lock held, then finalize cold mode under the mutex and release it before freeing the NCI device. Keep firmware-work handling unchanged. Actual C close/flush callbacks cover cold, open, firmware-state and optional-mode paths and reject the old locking. Concurrent firmware download remains unqualified.

nfc: nxp-nci: retain receive IRQ until the closing NCI reset finishes

NCI unregister sends CORE_RESET while the controller is up. Releasing the I2C IRQ before unregister prevents receiving its response; the request times out even though nci_close_device returns success.

Add an optional transport stop_rx operation. Unregister with receive still available, then stop and drain receive outside info_lock before the final cold-mode cleanup and nci_free_device. The I2C hook releases only an IRQ that request_threaded_irq successfully registered, so probe error unwind does not free an unowned IRQ.

An extracted-C test includes actual NCI reset, close, unregister, frame receive and reset-response code, actual I2C probe/send/read/IRQ/remove and core open/close/send/remove. Ten modeled cases pass under address/undefined-behavior sanitizers; r58 and five broken order/lock/wiring/ownership controls fail. Three ARM objects compile with W=1 and CFI retained. These host results do not qualify hardware timing or concurrent firmware download. The changed private operations type requires rebuilding matching modules; no candidate package has been built or installed.
